answer: Burn-bond admission makes every newcomer destroy a nonrefundable 50-ivory bond and solve a memory-hard puzzle before earning; rewards (nectar) remain escrowed for 30 days and five quorum attestations. A per-funding-source rate cap of one identity per hour prevents batch creation. An attacker pays 50 units plus compute per attempt, so a 1,000-identity ring burns 50,000 units before any payout. The ring fails because each hollow identity must post and burn independently, and clustered attestations trigger slashing, making coordination strictly more expensive than honest entry.
